findings.claim: E-003 full regression is confirmed solely by a single environment-provided selftest log with per-suite pass/fail summaries and no per-test detail.
findings.recommended_action: Attach per-suite verbose selftest output or replay artifacts, or re-run selftests under independent observation.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] The log is an environment artifact generated by the changed tools; per evidence discipline it cannot alone confirm behavior. The one-line-per-suite format could hide failures or skipped tests, and does not show that the new cookie-deletion, active-pointer, Coda, and closure-gate paths were exercised.

findings.claim: The aggregate frozen diff `reviewed.diff` referenced in E-004 is not present in the review bundle, so its SHA1 cannot be independently recomputed from the supplied component diffs.
findings.recommended_action: Include the aggregate `reviewed.diff` in the bundle or provide a reproducible `git diff` command output signed by the base commit.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] The manifest states the aggregate is intentionally omitted to avoid truncation. An external reviewer can verify the listed component SHA1s but cannot verify that their union equals the claimed aggregate SHA1 `4d8a55e7...`.

findings.claim: output_gate.py permits a generic `下一行动:` when the active-front set is empty but the run is not marked complete, because the front-id/control-plane requirement is only enforced when active_fronts is non-empty.
findings.recommended_action: Add a guard: if loop_complete is false and active_fronts is empty, require the Coda to reference a canonical control-plane object or to repair/read frontier.md; do not accept arbitrary concrete actions.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] In the fallback state (loop_state import failure or empty frontier), `_protocol_block_reason` only requires a syntactically valid Coda when no active fronts exist. This could allow a turn to end without advancing the run or resolving the missing state.

findings.claim: check_run.py's legacy free-form independent-review path can be satisfied by long self-review prose containing adjudication keywords, without a real reviewer identity or verdict.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the legacy free-form exception or restrict it to pre-existing reviews with a verified backend marker; require structured Reviewer + Verdict for all new closures.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] The condition `len(compact) >= 600 and re.search(... 'BLOCKER' ... 'False-positive')` is heuristic; a driver could paste a long self-review containing those tokens and pass the independent-review gate, undermining the new hard requirement.

findings.claim: run_gate.py's fallback `_has_codex_completion_review` regex can match a driver-written prose line, allowing a closure to bypass a fresh-context Codex completion review when the canonical check_run parser is unavailable.
findings.recommended_action: Make run_gate fail closed when the canonical check_run parser is unavailable, instead of using a permissive regex fallback.
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] [arkcli:kimi-k2.7-code] The function first tries check_run.has_codex_completion_review, but if `_cr` is None it falls back to a regex that accepts a manually written `- CodexCompletionReview: PASS` line. This contradicts the stated intent that only a fresh codex agent can write that review.

findings.why: [panel:arkcli] At least one arkcli reviewer failed, so PASS only means the completed panel members found no blocker.

blind_spots: [arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] No independent re-execution of the selftests was performed; the bundle contains only a high-level log.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] The `docs.diff` template/reference changes are not exercised by any visible targeted selftest output (only the generic `check_templates` suite is listed).

[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] There is no evidence that the active-run pointer file is actually created/updated by `setup_run.py` or `loop_bootstrap.py` in a real loop; the anti_drift selftest uses a temporary pointer.
[arkcli] [kimi-k2.7-code] Coverage_matrix's new behavior for mention-only verdicts is unit-tested, but no integration evidence shows it interacting with a real frontier/evidence/report set.

[claude] **The `output_gate.py` → `run_gate.py` integration selftest covers only one closure-blocking scenario**: The selftest at `output_gate.diff:342-357` tests that when all fronts are closed but independent review is missing, output_gate passes the Coda `下一行动: 运行 check_run 收口检查` and run_gate blocks with "缺独立复审". This proves the explicit-pointer pipeline works for ONE blocking reason. But it doesn't test: (a) missing CodexCompletionReview blocking, (b) open fronts blocking, (c) missing retrospective proof blocking. These other gates are tested at the unit level in `run_gate.py` selftest but not end-to-end through the hook pipeline.

[claude] **`CODA_RE` with `(?im)` flags and `$` anchor**: The `$` matches end-of-line in multiline mode. Combined with the `match.end() != len(clean)` check at output_gate.diff line 37, this ensures the Coda must be the last line. But if the model emits `下一行动: F-001 检查登录

` (trailing newline after the Coda), would this be rejected? The `rstrip()` at line 30 removes trailing whitespace including newlines, so `

` would be stripped — the match.end() would equal len(clean). But if the model emits `下一行动: F-001 检查登录

Some trailing prose`, the `rstrip()` only removes whitespace, not the prose, so match.end() != len(clean) → rejected. ✓

[claude] **`_merge_cookies_into_headers` default behavior (explicit Cookie header > jar)**: `probe.diff:95-97` — when `prefer_cookies=False` (default), the explicit `Cookie` header overrides same-name jar cookies. This is the correct browser-equivalent behavior (the request's own Cookie header is what the client chose to send). The selftest at `probe.diff:253-257` proves this. ✓

[claude] **Cookie jar atomic write**: `probe.diff:79-86` — uses `NamedTemporaryFile` + `chmod 0o600` + `Path.replace()` (atomic on POSIX). On macOS the default tempfile mode is already 0o600. On Linux with permissive umask, there's a TOCTOU window before `chmod`. The deployment target is macOS, so this is an accepted platform limitation. The selftest at `probe.diff:244-245` validates the permission after write. ✓

[claude] **The `_fallback_protocol_state` frontier parser only matches H2-H6 headings** (`output_gate.diff:112`: `#{2,6}`). If a front uses H1 (unusual), it won't be counted in the fallback. In practice all run fronts use H3+, so this is low-risk.

[claude] **The 7 rounds of review progressively tightened the gates**: Round 3 found vague Coda bypasses → fixed. Round 4 found multi-action conjunction gaps (`和`, bare `and`) → fixed. Round 5 found verb-list gaps, timezone-naive expiry, `fresh-context` heading spoof → all fixed. Round 6 was a packaging fix (split the monolithic diff). Round 7 found run_gate review fallback degradation → fixed (fail-closed). The iterative hardening is thorough. My WARN findings above are residual edge cases that survived this process.

[claude] **No finding in the code changes is a safety regression**: Every change either adds new enforcement (stricter Coda, stricter review gates, per-item retrospective proof) or fixes behavior bugs (cookie precedence, deletion, atomic writes, coverage mention-only verdicts). Nothing weakens an existing safety boundary.
